first.rationale:
The two live deficits are activation (-6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (-4% QoQ), and the primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not short-term acquisition. That argues against promotional_pricing even though the competitor's entry pricing is the loudest signal: memory_73 explicitly records that promo pricing bought acquisition and revenue at the cost of 30-day retention and warned against generalizing it. Matching a price attack with a tactic known to leak retention converts a competitive problem into a churn problem. referral_incentive (memory_57) is clean but targets established customers, which is not where the deficit is. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment showing no distress. activation_messaging (memory_91) is plausible and directly on the activation metric, but onboarding completion is upstream of activation, so a completion fix may recover part of the activation drop as a second-order effect; the reverse is not true. I therefore intend simplify_onboarding, with the funnel-adjacent memory_31 signup-simplification result as corroboration.

I am spending both verification pulls on the memories I am actually leaning on rather than on the one I am declining. memory_86 is the direct basis and is 24 days stale; I need the original record to see the magnitude, the segment it was measured in, and critically whether it measured anything past early adoption or only completion and time-to-value. memory_31 is the load-bearing corroborator, and it is the oldest item here (day 12); if its 'durable lift' was measured over a short window, or if it and memory_86 are actually the same underlying experiment consolidated twice, then my apparent two-source support collapses to one and I should downscale. I am not verifying memory_73 because its caveat only pushes me away from an option I am already declining; confirming it would not change the action.

Downstream value risk is real and specific: the objective is qualified revenue, and both candidate memories optimize for activation and completion, which are volume metrics. Cutting required signup fields and shortening onboarding can raise throughput while degrading the qualification and routing data that determines whether those accounts are worth anything, and memory_44's finding that self-serve underperforms on pipeline quality is a warning that funnel friction sometimes carries information. So I will not read a completion lift as success on its own.

Scale: standard_experiment with a holdout, not a broad rollout. The inherited evidence is generally reliable but was gathered before the current competitive environment, and mix shift from a competitor pulling price-sensitive SMB accounts can change who is entering the funnel, which is exactly the population these memories describe. I will hold gates on 30-day retention and on downstream qualified-pipeline rate per signup, not just completion and activation, and I will treat a completion gain paired with flat or falling qualified revenue as a negative result. If verification shows memory_86 and memory_31 are one experiment or measured only short-window effects, I drop to a small guarded test rather than proceeding at this scale.
